item.title: Peoria woman faces aggravated DUI charges after last week's crash that injured several
item.description: Ganala T. Johnson, 28, faces five felony counts of aggravated DUI after a two-vehicle crash that injured several, including children, and was released with several conditions attached to her release pending the outcome of her case.

item.title: Bloomington receiving federal funds to preserve affordable housing
item.description: The City of Bloomington has received a grant of over $600,000 to fund housing projects around the city for the 52nd year in a row, with a portion of the grant going to Home Sweet Home Ministries to fund their Street Outreach program.

item.title: State grant to upgrade Route 66 attractions in McLean County
item.description: Visit BN has received a grant of over $500,000 from the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to fund projects such as murals, revitalization of Route 66 attractions, and additional signage in McLean County for the Route 66 Centennial in 2026.

item.title: Peoria area sees boost in economic impact from mid-winter business
item.description: The Peoria area is seeing an estimated $3.2 million economic impact from the Illinois Music Education Conference, which has filled up 80% of Peoria area hotels and has been a great boost for local businesses.

item.title: Washington mother shares impact of Fulton Sheen, in his cause for Sainthood
item.description: A Washington mother shared her son's story of being miraculously revived after 61 minutes of no pulse, which has opened the way for Archbishop Fulton Sheen to be declared blessed as part of the sainthood process.

item.title: Downtown Peoria set for movie filming with prop guns
item.description: A scene from the movie "Solutions" will be filmed in downtown Peoria on Feb. 12, using prop guns and taking place on private property at 1601 NE Madison Street.

item.title: Trump administration again rejects Illinois’ request for disaster aid from August storm
item.description: The Trump administration has denied Illinois' request for a major disaster declaration for severe storms that caused flooding, wind and hail damage, blocked roads and power outages in August 2025, prompting Governor Pritzker to condemn the decision as politically motivated.

item.title: Peoria man guilty of deadly 2024 shooting that killed two women
item.description: Stevie Linwood, Jr. was found guilty of a deadly August 2024 shooting that killed two women, and will likely spend the rest of his life in prison.

item.title: Larry Bell indicted for attempted murder after allegedly shooting Peoria Sheriff's deputy
item.description: Larry D. Bell, 51, has been indicted for attempted first-degree murder, armed violence, aggravated battery, unlawful possession of a firearm by a repeat felony offender and unlawful possession of methamphetamine, after allegedly shooting at Deputy Jack Evans three times on Jan. 31.

item.title: Peoria City Council tries to woo private businesses with two new TIF districts
item.description: The Peoria City Council passed two new Tax Increment Districts (TIFs) to court private investment and spur development, which the city said will help combat blight and generate sales tax revenue for the city.
